extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers (news consumers) and newspaper editors/reporters
extracted.subtask_description: A wire-service/press dispatch reporting combat actions, military movements, casualties, and eyewitness accounts from a wartime front. Emphasizes dateline/location, source attribution, and a mix of official communiqués and on-the-scene detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute sources and indicate confirmation level
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute information to named sources and label its confirmation status (examples in text: 'Associated Press correspondent Tom Lambert reported...', 'A Tokyo Air Headquarters spokesman said...', 'UNCONFIRMED REPORTS').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear attribution verbs ('reported', 'said', 'announced') and explicitly flag unverified material ('unconfirmed reports', 'could not determine until all reports were in'). When possible, name the correspondent, headquarters, or official and indicate if information is preliminary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include dateline, location, and timestamp
rubrics_metrics.description: Start dispatches with a clear dateline and time/location marker (examples: 'TOKYO, TUESDAY, JULY 4-(AP)-', 'SOMEWHERE IN SOUTH KOREA, TUESDAY, JULY 4-(AP)-').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the dateline at the top to orient readers to where and when the events or reporting took place; repeat location context in text when moving between fronts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use on-the-scene correspondent eyewitness detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate vivid, specific observations from correspondents on the ground (example: Roy McCartney 'dived for a river bank and snuggled up under the bank's ...', 'lost his glasses in the dive for cover').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sensory, action-oriented details and short anecdotal moments to convey immediacy and the atmosphere of the scene without overshadowing factual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report casualty lists with names, ranks, and hometowns; protect next-of-kin
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide names, ranks and home addresses for casualties when available, but withhold names pending notification ('The name of the wounded sergeant was withheld pending notification of kin').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish full identifying details for killed/missing only when cleared by authorities or next-of-kin procedures; otherwise note status and any official casualty-list releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present uncertainties and conflicting accounts; avoid asserting unverified facts
rubrics_metrics.description: When accounts conflict or data are incomplete, report the different versions and note lack of confirmation (examples: 'He could not determine what happened until all of Monday's air strike reports were in and assayed', 'unconfirmed reports').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple or contradictory sources exist, attribute each version and explicitly state uncertainty rather than synthesizing an unsupported single narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on and cite official communiqués and headquarters statements for operational claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Use formal military communiqués and headquarters announcements as the basis for operational claims (examples: 'The communique issued by General MacArthur's headquarters said...', 'Headquarters announced that Australian fighter planes have joined American aircraft').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the issuing body and summarize claims from the communique, but if the communique lacks detail, make that limitation clear to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe equipment, aircraft types, and insignia to identify forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide technical/visual identifiers (plane models, markings) to clarify which forces were involved (examples: 'identified the planes as F-51 Mustangs', 'a white dot inside a blue circle', 'red, white and blue circles without a central dot').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give distinguishing details (model names, insignia descriptions) to reduce confusion about identities of forces; when identification is uncertain, state that uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include strategic movement, logistics, and damage assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Report troop movements, concentrations, rail and supply disruptions, and damage tallies (examples: 'troop trains shuttling', 'an ammunition dump was blown up', 'twenty-nine enemy trucks and five tanks listed as damaged').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specifics about locations, directions, and the tactical/logistical effects of actions; attribute assessments to sources or communiqués and note when damage counts are preliminary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include human-interest and reaction details to humanize the report
rubrics_metrics.description: Interleave human reactions and small personal moments within operational reporting (examples: a wounded sergeant 'grinned... and yelled: "SANYONE GOT ANY LETTERS THEY WANT ME TO TAKE HOME?"', soldiers 'dived for cover like veterans').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short quotes, reactions and personal anecdotes to balance technical/military facts and convey emotional context, while keeping them clearly delineated from factual claims.
